oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationExpiration.msgFail: Device code TTL must be between 60 and 3600 seconds
oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationExpiration.documentation: OpenID Connect Device Authorization code TTL (RFC 8628), between 60 and 3600 seconds

oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationPollingInt.msgFail: Polling interval must be between 1 and 60 seconds
oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationPollingInt.documentation: OpenID Connect Device Authorization polling interval (RFC 8628), between 1 and 60 seconds

oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationUserCodeLe.msgFail: User code length must be between 8 and 20 characters
oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationUserCodeLe.documentation: OpenID Connect Device Authorization user code length (RFC 8628). Minimum 8: over the 20-character alphabet that is ~34 bits of entropy, above the 20 bits RFC 8628 section 6.1 asks for

oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationMaxFailure.msgFail: Maximum invalid user codes must be between 0 and 100
oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationMaxFailure.documentation: Number of invalid user codes a single SSO session may submit before device verification is locked for that session (0 disables the lockout)

oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationLockoutDel.msgFail: Lockout delay must be between 30 and 3600 seconds
oidcServiceDeviceAuthorizationLockoutDel.documentation: How long device verification stays locked for a session that submitted too many invalid user codes, in seconds

oidcRPMetaDataOptionsAllowDeviceAuthoriz.documentation: Enable Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628). 1 lets ANY authenticated user approve an enrollment for this RP; use a rule (e.g. $groups =~ /\bdeviceadmins\b/) to restrict who may approve
